recipes.name: Easy Peanut Butter Chocolate Chip Cookies

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease two cookie sheets.

Beat butter and both sugars in a bowl with an electric mixer until creamy. Add egg and vanilla; mix until well combined. Mix in peanut butter, baking soda, and salt until fully incorporated. Mix in flour, then stir in chocolate chips.
Drop spoonfuls of dough 2 inches apart onto the prepared baking sheets; flatten slightly with a fork.

Bake in the preheated oven until just starting to turn golden brown on the edges, 5 to 6 minutes; don't overcook. Cool on the cookie sheets for 5 to 10 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to finish cooling.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Peanut Butter Chocolate Chip Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These easy peanut butter chocolate chip cookies made with natural peanut butter are simple to make and ready in just 30 minutes.

review.reviewBody: This is the best PB recipe I have ever used. I used just regular peanut butter and regular choc. chips. Which worked out perfectly! You will see that the cookies will turn out chewy and tastful!

I have made these cookies a million times and they are always a hit! I use some organic ingredients such as sugar, eggs, flour, and vanilla extract. I used regular "light" peanut butter, extra vanilla extract, and about 10% less sugar. MAKE SURE YOU LEAVE THE BUTTER OUT OF THE FRIDGE LONG ENOUGH!! this is key! I also use a digital weight scale for measurements. Also sift the flour! It makes a huge difference! If you don't have a sifter, tap out the flour from a spoon because it is all packed and heavy from the packaging and time. I also bake them for longer, approx 7-9 minutes. P.S. Barb, whoever you are, thank you for this recipe!

Great simple recipe! I used 1/4 C almond flour with 1/2 C regular flour. I also added 1/2 tsp instant coffee granules into the butter batter. I dipped the fork in sugar when making the crosses on top before baking.

Great recipe! The cookies turn out soft, chewy and a tiny bit crumbly. Not too sweet either! I used regular pb and added an extra 1/4 cup of flour. I also baked them for 8 mins (but that might be due to my silpat mat). I’ll definitely make them again.

I was hesitant to use this recipe because of the mixed reviews. I was pleasantly surprised. Followed recipe with these changes. I used 1 cup flour, 1/2 cup of each of the sugars and 1/2 the salt since I used salted butter. I used the on sale regular peanut butter. I used wax paper for the first pan and non-stick spray for second. Both worked well. If you have only one pan, I suggest using the paper so you can let the cookies cool on the paper while using the pan again. I also put the batter in freezer about 30 min before baking and returned to freezer between. Don't flatten out too much. I elected to not mix in the chips since I like without and put about 7 chips on the top of each cookie before baking for some of them. They were perfect both with and without. I baked them for 9 minutes and still they didn't look quite ready, but once cooled, they were perfect. The secret to these guys is to let them cool about 10min before trying to remove from the pan or paper. I will be making these again and will double the batch.

As others suggested, I used about 1 and 1/4 cup flour instead. I also melted the butter so it would be easier to mix. As others have also noted, the cookies will crumble if you don't wait for them to cool completely. I cooked them at 370 for about 9 minutes. Took them out when the edges were just barely brown. Perfect!! They are fluffy and peanut buttery... very yummy... will definitely make again!

So at first, this recipe made me nervous based on the comments. For the first batch, I didn’t make any measuring adjustments and when the cookies came out of the oven, they were so, so soft that I figured they were ruined. I let them cool for 10 minutes on the sheet while chilling the remaining dough... I added 1 tbsp of flour to the remaining chilled dough and baked for 9 minutes... and? You can’t tell a difference between batch one and batch two! Lol! But... they are delicious! Will definitely make again. Used one cup natural honey roasted peanut butter and 1/3 cup dark chocolate almond butter and the flavor is ... just wow.

I made just a few changes. I did add a Full cup of flour and always am heavy handed with chocolate chips. Its necessary to hold the doug in the fridge for a minimum of 35 minutes. I rolled the cookie balls in white sugar before baking. They werè perfect and delish...

Soft, chewy and delicious! These are wonderfully yummy! (And, have no trans fats!) I followed the recipe almost exactly- just added 2 more tablespoons of flour and another 1/8 teaspoon kosher salt. Also instead of mixing in mini chips, I added three regular-sized chocolate chips to the center of each pb cookie after baking. For the crumbling problem- baking longer is not the answer!! I would recommend using insulated baking sheets and a good, thin, metal pancake turner to remove the cookies. Be sure to allow them to cool for 1-2 minutes before removing.

I made a double batch using Bob's Red Mill GF flower recipe for Choc chip cookies. 2c flour to 1c peanut butter. GF stuff can be dry so it has 2 eggs as well. Even the dough is amazing, which is unusual for GF flours. Highly recommend the change. Combine the recipes or just use this one with the flour. I don't think it can go wrong.

My roommates can't get enough of these. I add the extra 2 TBL spoons of flour, bake for 7 minutes per batch. My best finished product starts as a ball just under the size of a golf ball, rolled and then pressed to about 1/4" thick on the pan. They spread when they bake to about 1 1/2" their starting size. I also take 3 Skor bars, freeze them and then shatter them with a butter knife handle and mix in with the chocolate chips.
A great recipe for great cookies!!
Delicious!

I read them most of the comments and I find it interesting that so many people had problems with this recipe. I did, at the advice of other comments, add a little more flour under a quarter of a cup though. I’m not sure if that was necessary. The next time I make this recipe, I will do it as stated. Anyway, this recipe was delicious. The only other change I made is I prefer Hershey’s milk chocolate so I add a small piece of a chocolate bar after the cookies have come out of the oven. Let them melt and then swirl it around the top. Delicious.

If there were negative stars I would have chosen a few. I should have read the reviews before choosing this recipe. What a waste of ingredients. Yes I followed the recipe to a “T”. Cookie crumbs anyone?
Like many others, my cookies came out too soft and crumbly. I even measured the flour as the instructions advised.. I won't make this recipe again. I think it needed more flour.
Cookies did not come out right at all. I was so looking forward to these so that I could give them out for Christmas but I'm to worried people won't like them!

Easy, peasy! Taste great and made 24 perfect sized cookies. Depending on your affection for chocolate morsels, you may want to add a few. Teenagers agreed to take over the final steps, including the scarfing 😁☮️

I usually don't make Peanut Butter cookies but they looked too easy to resist. After reading the reviews I did round the flour to a cup and I didn't have Natural Peanut Butter. But the cookies came out really good. They melted in my mouth. I'll be making these again but probably add a few oats in them.
While they were easy to make they totally fell apart. Taste was fine but did not hold up as they were way to crumbly.
